content: 1. Disorders of tooth development and eruption refer to abnormalities in the formation or emergence of teeth. 2. Dental caries, also known as tooth decay, is the destruction of the hard tissues of the teeth caused by bacterial activity. 3. Diseases of the pulp and periapical tissues involve inflammation or infection of the dental pulp and surrounding structures. 4. Chronic gingivitis is a long-term inflammation of the gums, often caused by plaque buildup. 5. Dentofacial anomalies, including malocclusion, describe irregularities in the alignment of teeth and jaws. 6. Torus mandibularis and torus palatinus are benign bony growths in the lower jaw and palate, respectively. 7. Parotitis is an inflammation of the parotid salivary glands, which may be caused by infection or other factors. 8. Stomatitis refers to inflammation of the oral mucosa, which can result from infections, irritants, or systemic conditions. 9. Aphthous ulcers, commonly known as canker sores, are small, painful lesions in the oral mucosa. 10. Oral leukoplakia is a condition characterized by white patches on the mucous membranes of the mouth, which may be precancerous. 11. Erythroplakia is a red patch in the oral mucosa that carries a high risk of malignancy. 12. Glossitis is the inflammation of the tongue, often resulting in swelling, redness, and changes in texture. 13. Achalasia, also known as cardiospasm, is a disorder where the esophagus has difficulty moving food into the stomach due to impaired relaxation of the lower esophageal sphincter. 14. Esophagitis refers to inflammation of the esophagus, which can result from acid reflux, infections, or other causes. 15. Esophageal stricture or stenosis is the narrowing of the esophagus, which can lead to difficulty swallowing. 16. Gastroesophageal reflux without esophagitis involves the backflow of stomach contents into the esophagus without causing inflammation. 17. Barrett's esophagitis is a condition where the lining of the esophagus changes due to chronic acid reflux, increasing the risk of esophageal cancer. 18. Gastric ulcers are open sores that develop on the inner lining of the stomach. 19. Duodenal ulcers are open sores that occur in the first part of the small intestine, known as the duodenum. 20. Peptic ulcers are ulcers of the stomach or duodenum without a specified location. 21. Gastrojejunal ulcers are ulcers that occur at the site of a surgical connection between the stomach and the jejunum. 22. Acute gastritis is a sudden inflammation of the stomach lining, often caused by irritants such as alcohol or medications. 23. Duodenitis is inflammation of the duodenum, which may result from infections, medications, or other factors. 24. Gastroparesis is a condition where the stomach empties more slowly than normal due to impaired motility. 25. Dyspepsia, commonly referred to as indigestion, is a condition characterized by discomfort or pain in the upper abdomen. 26. Acute appendicitis is the sudden inflammation of the appendix, which may or may not involve generalized peritonitis. 27. Appendicitis with generalized peritonitis occurs when the inflamed appendix causes widespread infection in the abdominal cavity. 28. Appendicitis without peritonitis refers to inflammation of the appendix without spreading infection. 29. Unqualified appendicitis refers to cases of appendicitis without further specification. 30. Other appendicitis includes less common forms of inflammation of the appendix. 31. Other diseases of the appendix encompass conditions affecting the appendix that are not classified as appendicitis. 32. Inguinal hernia is the protrusion of abdominal contents through the inguinal canal, which may be unilateral and nonspecific. 33. Hernias of the abdominal cavity with gangrene involve tissue death due to compromised blood supply. 34. Hernias of the abdominal cavity with obstruction occur when the hernia blocks the passage of intestinal contents. 35. Femoral hernia is the protrusion of abdominal contents through the femoral canal, typically unilateral. 36. Umbilical hernia is the protrusion of abdominal contents through the umbilical area. 37. Ventral hernia is a protrusion through the abdominal wall, which may be unspecified or incisional. 38. Hiatal hernia is the protrusion of the stomach through the diaphragm into the chest cavity, typically noncongenital. 39. Other nonspecific hernias include various types of hernias not otherwise classified. 40. Crohn's disease of the small intestine is a chronic inflammatory condition affecting the small bowel. 41. Crohn's disease of the large intestine involves chronic inflammation of the colon. 42. Crohn's disease, not otherwise specified, refers to cases of Crohn's disease without further detail. 43. Idiopathic proctocolitis, including ulcerative colitis, is a chronic inflammatory condition of the colon and rectum. 44. Acute vascular insufficiency of the intestine occurs when blood flow to the intestines is suddenly reduced. 45. Ischemic bowel disease, unspecified, refers to conditions where the intestines are deprived of adequate blood supply. 46. Noninfectious gastroenteritis and colitis involve inflammation of the stomach and colon not caused by infection. 47. Intestinal obstruction without hernia refers to blockages in the intestines not associated with hernias. 48. Ileus is a condition where the intestines fail to move contents due to impaired motility. 49. Impaction of the intestine occurs when material becomes lodged in the intestines, causing obstruction. 50. Diverticulosis of the colon is the presence of small pouches in the colon wall, which may or may not cause symptoms. 51. Diverticulitis of the colon involves inflammation or infection of these pouches. 52. Diverticulosis with hemorrhage refers to bleeding associated with diverticulosis. 53. Constipation is the infrequent or difficult passage of stools. 54. Irritable bowel syndrome is a functional gastrointestinal disorder characterized by abdominal pain and altered bowel habits. 55. Post-gastric-surgery syndromes refer to complications following stomach surgery. 56. Postoperative functional disorders involve impaired digestive function after surgery. 57. Anal spasm is the involuntary contraction of the anal sphincter muscles. 58. 59. Perianal abscess is a collection of pus near the anus. 60. Peritonitis is inflammation of the peritoneum, the lining of the abdominal cavity. 61. Peritoneal adhesions are bands of scar tissue that form between abdominal organs. 62. Pneumoperitoneum is the presence of air or gas in the peritoneal cavity. 63. Rectal bleeding refers to the passage of blood from the rectum. 64. Infection of a colostomy or enterostomy involves inflammation or infection at the site of a surgical opening. 65. Mechanical complications of ostomies include blockages or other issues with the surgical opening. 66. Angiodysplasia of the intestine with hemorrhage is a condition where abnormal blood vessels in the intestines cause bleeding. 67. Acute hepatic failure is the sudden loss of liver function. 68. Alcoholic fatty liver is the accumulation of fat in the liver due to excessive alcohol consumption. 69. Alcoholic cirrhosis is the scarring of the liver caused by long-term alcohol abuse. 70. Chronic hepatitis, unspecified, refers to long-term liver inflammation without further detail. 71. Cirrhosis, not otherwise specified, is the scarring of the liver from various causes. 72. Primary biliary cirrhosis is a chronic autoimmune disease that damages the bile ducts in the liver. 73. Chronic liver disease, unspecified, refers to long-term liver conditions without further specification. 74. Hepatic coma is a severe complication of liver disease characterized by altered mental status due to liver failure. 75. Hepatorenal syndrome is a condition where severe liver disease leads to kidney failure. 76. 77. Choledocholithiasis is the presence of gallstones in the bile duct. 78. Acute cholecystitis is the sudden inflammation of the gallbladder, often due to gallstones. 79. Gallbladder disease, unspecified, refers to conditions affecting the gallbladder without further detail. 80. Cholangitis is the inflammation of the bile ducts, often due to infection. 81. Obstruction of the bile duct, including Mirizzi's syndrome, occurs when the bile duct is blocked, leading to bile flow impairment. 82. Acute pancreatitis is the sudden inflammation of the pancreas. 83. Chronic pancreatitis is long-term inflammation of the pancreas, often leading to permanent damage. 84. Pancreatic pseudocyst is a fluid-filled sac in the pancreas that develops after inflammation or injury. 85. Hematemesis is the vomiting of blood, often indicating gastrointestinal bleeding. 86. Melena is the passage of dark, tarry stools due to the presence of digested blood. 87. Coeliac disease is an autoimmune disorder where ingestion of gluten damages the small intestine. 88. Malabsorption, not otherwise specified, refers to impaired nutrient absorption without further detail.
